content.text: {"headline":"No action needed: both queues are predicted to stay above the 80% target through 11:00-13:00 (91.2% overall).","why":"General is running 28.4% above forecast (617 calls vs 480.4) for no identified reason, but staffing matches plan with no absences against 47 rostered. Even so, the model predicts 91.2% service level for the disruption window (payments 91.1%, general 91.4%), with 2.7% abandons and 93.0% for the rest of the day. That clears the 80% target at zero cost, so no intervention is required.","trade_offs":["P2 (chat deflection of balance enquiries plus callbacks) predicts slightly better results: 91.8% service level and 2.2% abandons vs 2.7%, for ₹168. It is a small gain if you want extra margin.","P1 (no cost: break delays, callbacks, moving 2 agents from payments) predicts worse results than doing nothing: 88.5% service level, with payments falling to 87.8% and abandons rising to 3.3%.","P3 (overtime) costs ₹4,140 and still predicts worse results in the window: 88.2% service level, with payments down to 86.4%. It is not worth it."],"watch":"The surge is unexplained, so keep tracking General volume against forecast each interval. Watch login_issue closely (96 vs 58.9 expected, 1.63x): it may point to an unreported login problem. If volume keeps climbing, revisit P2 as the low-cost fallback."}
